tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: Level 1 starts, on the loadout screen.

pages.text: Hi! Nice to meet you, I'm the Acorn Knight. I'm here to help you learn how to play the game!
First, let's learn how to select a plant.
Hover over me in the Available Plants section. You should get a preview of what I'm able to do! Then, click on me to select me. Once that's done, I'll move up to the Current Loadout section.
Great! Now that I'm selected, click on the Next button.

tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: Level 1, when the fertilizer screen opens (the game is already paused there).

pages.text: After choosing your team of plants, you get to pick one Fertilizer which grants you a bonus that can change the way a level plays out!
Select the Fertilizer you wish to benefit from!

tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: Level 1, right after a fertilizer is picked, in the setup phase before the first wave.

pages.text: Now that the level has started, you can see the selected plants in the top right corner of the screen.
Click on me (or Press 1) , that'll select me. Then, place me on any Dirt tile on the map!
pages.note: here, the player is expected to select the acorn knight , and place it on any dirt tile in the map, once that's done, jump to next tutorial text

pages.text: Hold on, my mistake! You shouldn't place me on a Dirt Tile! Click on the Shovel on the right side of the screen, and then select the Acorn Knight you just placed on the Dirt Tile!
pages.note: here, the player is expected to select the shovel, and then remove the acorn from the field, once thats done, move to next

pages.text: When you Shovel a plant, you get a 50% refund of all the Sun spent on it. However, since we're still in the Setup Phase, you get 100%. Now select me once again (or Press 1), and place me on a Grass Tile!
pages.note: player is expected to select the acorn knight again, and then place it on a grass tile

pages.text: Awesome! So, since I'm a Grass element plant, I can be placed on Grass Tiles. On top of that, we Grass element plants get a bonus point in our Passive Tree which increases the effectiveness of what makes us unique!
Wonderful, now we're ready to start the level! Click on the START button at the bottom right of your screen (or press Space) to begin!

tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: Level 1, once wave 1's second group has started and you have more than 18 Sun.

pages.text: For more information on what I can do, click on the placed Acorn Knight.
pages.note: the player is expected to click on the acorn knight placed then next tutorial proceeds

pages.text: You can hover over my portrait to see my General Information
pages.note: the player is expected to hover over the acorn knight's icon in the plant info panel then next tutorial proceeds

pages.text: On the right side of that, you can see my Basic Combat Stats and if you hover over it, you'll be able to see additional details regarding my stats. You could also see active Status Effects! Except, I don't have any right now so you won't see anything. Ha!
pages.note: the player is expected to hover over the statspanel then next tutorial proceeds

pages.text: Below that, you'll see the Attack, Passive and Skill paths! Hover over any of them to see that intricacies of what I have to offer!
pages.note: the player is expected to hover over either the attack, or passive, or skill tree, once at least one is done, proceed tutorial

pages.text: I notice that you have enough Sun to upgrade something! Let's upgrade the Attack tree by clicking on the upgrade button next to the Attack tree!
pages.note: the player is expected to upgrade the attack path, once done, proceed tutorial, during this time, CANNOT upgrade anything else.

pages.text: Great! Now that the Attack tree is upgraded, I'm a little bit more powerful! If you look below, you'll notice that the Passive Tree has an extra level. Remember? It's because you placed me on a Grass Tile!
pages.note: player can click on the panel to close the tutorial.

tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: Level 1, the first time a mulch drops.
tutorials.comment: shown the first time a mulch drops in level 1 (MulchManager.OnDropSpawned), game paused. page 3 waits for the player to take the drop (TutorialEvents.TakeMulch: clicked or dragged into the bag, or dragged onto a plant); a drop can be taken mid hop, so pausing doesn't block it

pages.text: Insects sometimes drop Mulches when slain! These are little bags with cute glitter around them.

Mulches are going to be your friends in the garden, they grant a plant various bonuses that could really help them defend your garden! You can hover over them to see what kind of bonus they can provide.
Click on it to add it in your Mulch Inventory, or you could actually drag it on your plant! Your inventory will serve as storage for mulches you wish to save or to use later in the level.
pages.note: here, the player is expected to either click on the mulch to add it to the inventory OR drag it to a plant OR the inventory.

pages.text: BUT! You should know that the mulches don't carry over from level to level!

A plant can hold up to 6 mulches, and so can you. Two identical mulches of the same rarity will merge into a stronger one. If a mulch seems uninteresting, right click on it to sell it! You can only sell mulches that are in your inventory.

tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: 4 seconds after the first Soldier Ant ever spawns.
tutorials.comment: player is not expected to do anything, but simply read the tutorial and click to proceed, but the game is paused and non-unpausable while this tutorial holds active

pages.text: So this is a Soldier Ant. It's a tougher variant of an ant that's like suuuuuper duuuuper bulky and takes reduced damage from Physical AND Grass attacks! I'm not really the best plant to fight this ant.
They're also mildly aggressive, meaning that they walk off the path to attack us!
Here's where I shine! So, you know how every plant has a passive? Yeah, well mine allows me to raise my shield, entering a Guard Stance whenever I sense that an insect sees me as their target!
While I'm holding up my shield, I have increased Armor, and my attacks change to a Shield Bash, which doesn't benefit from my Attack Damage, but rather my Armor!

So, when the Soldier Ant attacks a plant, he hits once, then continues on its way. Another cool thing about my passive is that insects that target me won't leave after hitting me. I'm able to hold their attention while other plants tear them down!

tutorials.speaker: Sunflower
tutorials.trigger: Level 2, right after a fertilizer is picked, if Sunflower is in the loadout.
tutorials.comment: triggers the moment the player enters level 2's setup phase (the initial pre-level fertilizer selection), same hook point as Level1StartLevel - see FertilizerSelectionUI

pages.text: Hiya! I'm the Sunflower. I'm happy to meet you!
Click on me, that'll select me. Then, place me on any Dirt Tile on the map!
pages.note: player is expected to select the sunflower and place her on any dirt tile, once done, proceed tutorial

pages.text: See, unlike the Acorn Knight, I'm a Fire plant, so I can't be placed on Grass Tiles. We Fire plants do however benefit from a Sunny Weather. So, we get an extra Passive point whenever we're exposed to the sun!
I can help you defend the garden in many ways! My fireballs deal Fire Magic Damage, so I'm really the perfect solution to the tough Soldier Ants!

As for my passive, I produce Sun as time passes, so you'll be able to place and upgrade more plants as long as I'm on the field! Landing shots with my fireballs also reduces the cooldown on my sun generation!
And finally my skill allows me to gather fire energy and shoot down a Sunray, a beam that deals continuous Fire damage!
pages.note: player can click on the panel to close the tutorial.

tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: Level 2, 1 second after the first elemental primer lands on an insect.
tutorials.comment: triggers the moment any plant inflicts an elemental primer on an insect for the first time (see ElementalDebuff.OnApply) - purely informational, no action required

pages.text: Notice the elemental icon above that insect? That means it's being primed with an Elemental Debuff! If another elemental attack lands on it while primed, it triggers an Elemental Reaction!
In our case, whenever Grass comes in contact with Fire, it starts a Burn effect on the target, dealing Magic Fire damage over time!
pages.note: player can click on the panel to close the tutorial.

tutorials.speaker: Waterlily
tutorials.trigger: Level 3, right after a fertilizer is picked, if Waterlily is in the loadout.
tutorials.comment: triggers the moment the player enters level 3's setup phase (the initial pre-level fertilizer selection), same hook point as Level1StartLevel/Level2StartLevel - see FertilizerSelectionUI

pages.text: Hi! I'm Waterlily, soooo nice to meet you!
Click on me, that'll select me. Then, place me on any Water tile on the map! Yup, I'm an aquatic plant so I can only be placed on Water.
pages.note: player is expected to select the waterlily and place her on any water tile, once done, proceed tutorial

pages.text: I shoot slow-moving bubbles that deal Water Magic Damage to insects in an area around the impact!
My passive makes it so that my attacks inflict Soaked on insects, which Slows them down but also grounds flying insects!
My skill lets me shoot a huge bubble that deals damage and traps insects in place while keeping them airborne!
pages.note: player can click on the panel to close the tutorial.

tutorials.speaker: AcornKnight
tutorials.trigger: Level 1, from 4 seconds into wave 3, once an Acorn Knight's skill is still locked and you have the Sun to unlock it. Until then level 1 keeps skills locked.
tutorials.comment: level 1, from 4 seconds into wave 3, once there is an Acorn Knight whose skill is still locked and enough sun to unlock it (see ProceduralLevel.Update), game paused. until then level 1 keeps every skill locked (TutorialManager.Level1SkillLocked). page 1 waits for the unlock, page 2 for the thrown shield to land: the game runs from the throw until it lands (AcornKnight)

pages.text: Things are about to get rough. All plants also have a Skill, but they need to be unlocked, so you just gotta click on the vines to unlock my skill.
pages.note: here, the player is expected to click on the skill unlock vines to unlock the skill. note that before this tutorial, the player should NOT be able to unlock the skill.

pages.text: You can cast my skill by clicking on me, then clicking on the Skill Icon or just by Pressing "Q" as a shortcut, then you'll have to aim and click with your mouse to cast it!
pages.note: here, the player is expected to cast the acorn skill. the game runs from the cast until the shield lands (AcornKnight), then pauses again for page 3

pages.text: My skill allows me to throw my shield in a straight line, dropping on the ground when it reaches the destination or it hits an insect. It deals damage, and stuns for a little bit, but it stays on the ground, blocking the path, so insects have no choice but to munch on my shield.
pages.note: shown once the thrown shield has landed on the ground

pages.text: I just won't be able to hold a Guard Stance while my shield is on the floor, so I will be vulnerable. Just remember that... Please.

tutorials.speaker: Waterlily
tutorials.trigger: The first time a Waterlily puts a Water primer on an insect, 1 second after it lands.
tutorials.comment: the first time a Waterlily puts a Water primer on an insect, 1 second after it lands (see ElementalDebuff.OnApply), game paused. click through pages only

pages.text: Just like the other plants, my attacks also apply a Water primer to react with the other elements!

Whenever Water reacts with Grass, it Germinates for a few seconds, then blooms, dealing Grass Physical Damage in an area. Whenever it reacts with Fire, it Steams, reducing Fire Resistance, Water Resistance, and Healing Received on the affected insect.
